title: Vorticella bells form a graded series of unduloids

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Vorticella bells form a graded series of unduloids

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The bells of the various species of Vorticella, like many other Infusoria, are unduloids or partial unduloids spanning every gradation from nearly cylindrical to nearly spherical, bounded by the stalk attachment and the ciliary ring as by two unequal supporting rings, and the species differ only in ratio or degree.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. V: The Forms of Cells

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The cups of the various species of Vorticella (Fig. 75) are nothing in the world but a beautiful series of unduloids, or partial unduloids, in every gradation from a form that is all but cylindrical to one that is all but a perfect sphere.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter V, “The Forms of Cells”; topic “Unduloid forms of Infusoria”. Scope: Vorticella and other cup-shaped or flask-shaped ciliates and flagellates

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch05-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The surface family and claimed parameter continuum yield clear geometric model comparisons. Available public imagery likely tests some species but is insufficient for the asserted complete graded series.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Build calibrated 3D outlines of Vorticella bells, fit partial unduloids under the measured stalk and ciliary-ring boundaries, and compare fits with alternative constant-mean-curvature and flexible surfaces. Map fitted parameters across species to test for a continuous cylinder-to-sphere gradation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Species identification and boundary-ring dimensions may be missing.

Live contraction changes bell shape.

Most public images are 2D and not taxonomically balanced.

fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.85

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: An unduloid bounded by two rings is a specific curve family, so a fit to photographed bells can confirm or reject it for the species that have been drawn. There is no public coordinate dataset, and the taxonomic series would have to be built from plates. The mathematics is discriminating; the available images support only a partial, illustration-biased test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit Vorticella bell outlines to the unduloid family between two unequal end rings, the stalk junction and the ciliary ring, and test whether species form a continuous series from near-cylinder to near-sphere. A good unduloid fit across that series would support the claim; systematic residuals, or a better fit to another surface family, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Species sampling in illustrations favours distinctive bells.

Bell outlines are in monographs and scattered photographs, not a morphometric archive.

A two-dimensional silhouette under-determines a surface of revolution.
